title: "Finally, we won" Choi Byung-chan's decisive strike + national team star Shin Min-ha's rock-solid defense... Gangwon defeats Kuching at home to secure ACL2 "first victory"

 Choi Byung-chan (left) attempts a kick during the third match of Group H in the group stage of the 2026-2027 Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Champions League 2 (ACL2), held between Gangwon FC and Kuching City on the 29th at Gangneung High1 Arena. /Photo=Korea Professional Football League Gangwon FC secured its first victory in the tournament after three matches in the group stage of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Champions League 2 (ACL2).
 Led by manager Jeong Gyeong-ho, Gangwon defeated Kuching City (Malaysia) 1-0 in their home match on the 29th at Gangneung High1 Arena for the third round of Group H in the 2026-2027 ACL2 group stage, powered by a decisive goal from Choi Byung-chan in the 28th minute of the first half.
 Gangwon, which had entered the playoff for the higher-tier Champions League Elite (ACLE) as the fifth-placed team in last season's K League 2 but was relegated to ACL2 after losing 0-1 to Gamba Osaka (Japan), had previously swallowed their disappointment with a draw (0-0) against Kitchee SC (Hong Kong) in the first match and a loss (1-2) to Phnom Penh Crown (Cambodia) in the second. However, with this third-match victory, they recorded one win, one draw, and one loss, successfully turning the momentum around.
 On this day, Gangwon fielded Kim Gun-hee, Lee Seung-won, Kim Dae-won, Seo Min-woo, and Choi Byung-chan as starters. Shin Min-ha, a center back who recently received his first call-up to the national team under manager Roberto Moreno, also started and led the defensive line.
 In the 28th minute of the first half, Gangwon took the lead when Choi Byung-chan controlled a pass from Kang Jun-hyuk and finished with a shot. Struck by the blow, Kuching City saw James Okuosa attempt a threatening header during a corner kick scramble in the 38th minute of the first half, but it was blocked by goalkeeper Park Cheong-hyo's save.
 Entering the second half, Gangwon brought on Park Ho-young, Lee Eun-ho, Kim Dong-hyun, and Park Sang-hyuk in succession to solidify their lead. Although no additional goals were scored, including a header from Choi Byung-chan that went over the crossbar in the 26th minute of the second half, they maintained their one-goal advantage until the final whistle to secure three points at home.
 Gangwon will play their away match against Kuching City for the fourth round on November 5 at 9:15 p.m.
